title: Ongoing notification wakes up display every 5 minutes.
body:
I'm using a Google Pixel XL with Android 10 and it's quite hard to get the ongoing notification to not wake up the display every 5 minutes. I have to have xDrip's notification set to "silent" via Android's notification setting, or the display will wake. If the notification is set to "alerting" the display wakes. If I enable "use notification channels" in xDrip, it doesn't seem to help.

Having the notification set to "silent" is fine, but the problem is that Android sticks it to the bottom of the notification cards under a "silent notifications" section. Ideally I would like to be able to stick the xDrip notification to the top, so I can quickly see it, and the small number in the notification bar is always visible.

Basically, if the ongoing notification is set to anything other than "silent" in the Android system settings, every 5 minutes the ambient display on the phone will illuminate, showing the time and notification icons. It seems to also do this if I enable "use notification channels". Do you have a phone there you could try to recreate the behaviour on?

You can disable it: Look for Registry Notifications and see the channelID xdrip is using to display the glucose every 5 minutes. Now open Settings in your phone, look for xDrip app then Notifications. There look for the channelID and turn off Floating Notifications and Not show notifications in lock screen. If channelID is null, then change this in Ongoing Notifications.
I hope it works
